reference.method: sample-extreme closed form (support monotonicity); damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

not_refined.N: closed form or exhaustive enumeration (independently checked)

global.statement: With both coefficients free, a finite MLE exists for every nonempty positive integer sample. If any observation exceeds one, the endpoint $\hat N=\max_i x_i$ and the shape estimate are unique. All-ones data give $\hat N=1$ with every finite $s\ge0$ maximizing the likelihood. With $N>1$ held, the shape MLE is finite and unique unless all observations are one, when only an unattained point-mass supremum exists. With $N=1$ held the shape is unidentified. With shape held, the unique endpoint MLE is the sample maximum. Holding both coefficients leaves only likelihood evaluation on the retained support.
global.reason: At every finite shape, the normalizing sum strictly increases with $N$, so the smallest data-compatible endpoint maximizes the likelihood. For $N>1$, the shape score per observation is $E_{N,s}[\log X]-\overline{\log x}$, with derivative $-\operatorname{Var}_{N,s}(\log X)<0$. Its model mean tends to zero at infinity. The maximum is $s=0$ if $\overline{\log x}\ge\log(N!)/N$, and otherwise is the unique positive root, unless the empirical log mean is zero.
